headline: Solar marketing in Dwarka, Delhi: winning society rooftops and independent houses
card_text: How Dwarka installers can pitch group housing societies, reach independent-house owners in the villages and colonies around the sub-city, and beat national brands on local search.
intro:
Solar marketing in Dwarka, Delhi looks easy on paper: flat terraces, a planned sub-city, sunny summers and electricity bills that jump when every flat runs two ACs. In practice, most of Dwarka lives in multi-storey group housing societies, where no single resident owns the roof. The homes where one owner can say yes quickly sit mostly in the colonies and urban villages around the sectors.

So a Dwarka installer needs two separate plans: a committee sale for societies and a fast, local lead engine for independent houses. This guide covers both, along with the 2026 Delhi rules that change how you qualify leads. We know the area well, because our own office is at 124, Triveni Heights in Dwarka, and we run campaigns for solar EPCs across Delhi NCR.

sections.h2: Who actually buys rooftop solar in Dwarka
sections.html:
Dwarka's 29 sectors are dominated by cooperative group housing (CGHS) societies and DDA flats, with markets, schools, hospitals and institutional buildings in between. Around the sectors are older, denser areas such as Palam, Mahavir Enclave, Bindapur, Matiala, Pochanpur and Bagdola, where people live in independent houses and builder floors. Each group buys differently:

BuyerWho decidesSales cycleWhat they care about
CGHS and DDA societyManaging committee, then the general bodyWeeks to monthsCommon-area bill savings, roof waterproofing, maintenance, subsidy paperwork
Independent house or builder floor ownerThe owner (and whoever has roof rights)Days to a few weeksNet cost, system size, monthly bill after solar
Schools, hospitals, shops and officesOwner, trustee or finance headWeeksPayback, capex vs RESCO, downtime during install

Society flat owners will still fill in your forms. Unless your campaign is built to feed society proposals, most of those leads won't convert, so filter them early.

sections.h2: Dwarka facts to get right before you advertise
sections.html:
• The DISCOM is BSES Rajdhani (BRPL). It supplies Dwarka and most of south-west Delhi, so your landing page and quotes should explain BRPL's application and net-metering steps, not generic Delhi steps.
  • Societies here have done this before. BRPL launched its "Solarise Dwarka" aggregation programme for apartment complexes in 2018. In July 2026 the Delhi Chief Minister inaugurated a 500 kW plant at the Air Force and Naval Officers Enclave in Sector 7, reported at about ₹2 crore with roughly ₹1 crore in central and Delhi subsidy. Committees in nearby societies know about projects like that, so lead with proof and process, not with "what is solar".
  • Delhi's 2026 policy changed the maths. The Second Amendment to the Delhi Solar Energy Policy 2023 was notified in September 2026. The Delhi Solar Portal lists a state capital subsidy for homes of up to ₹26,000 per kW for the first 3 kW, capped at ₹78,000, on top of PM Surya Ghar. Group housing societies and RWAs can get up to ₹11,000 per kWp for common areas, up to 500 kWp, on top of central assistance for common facilities.
  • A free route exists for smaller users. Under the DISCOM-led trusteeship route, eligible households using up to around 400 units a month can get up to 3 kW at little or no cost. Heavier users and bigger systems go through the open vendor route, which is where an installer earns.
  • GBI is gone for new homes and societies. The generation-based incentive has been replaced by the upfront capital subsidy for new residential and GHS/RWA plants, so don't promise per-unit payments.

These figures can change. Check the Delhi Solar Portal and the PM Surya Ghar portal before you publish a number, and use the wording in our guide to PM Surya Ghar subsidy ads.

sections.h2: Local SEO for solar installers in Dwarka
sections.html:
Search "solar company in Dwarka" and you'll see national rooftop brands with city pages, installer locality pages and directory listings. A local installer can still win the Maps results and the clicks, because buyers want someone who can reach their roof the same day:

  1. Google Business Profile. Pick "solar energy company" or the closest primary category, add Dwarka and the surrounding colonies you serve as service areas, and post photos of real Dwarka installs every week with the sector or colony in the caption.
  2. Reviews that name the area. Ask every customer for a review after commissioning, and ask them to mention their sector or society. A steady flow matters more than a burst.
  3. One strong Dwarka page. On your website, create a page for rooftop solar in Dwarka that covers BRPL net metering, society projects, independent houses, the 2026 subsidy summary and three or four local project photos. Don't create thin pages for every sector with the same text.
  4. Answer local questions. FAQs such as "Can our CGHS society get a solar subsidy?" and "How long does BRPL net metering take?" match what people actually type.

Our local SEO services page explains how we set this up for service businesses.

sections.h2: Meta and Google ads for Dwarka independent houses
sections.html:
For paid ads, the fastest buyers are owners of independent houses and builder floors in and around Dwarka.

  • Target tightly. Use pin-drop radiuses around the colonies and villages you serve rather than "Delhi". Run society-awareness ads as a separate campaign so the numbers don't mix.
  • Ask qualifying questions in the form: Do you own the roof? Independent house, builder floor or society flat? Average monthly units or bill? Which colony or sector? The units question matters more in Delhi now, because a household under the free-route line may not need a paid vendor.
  • On Google Search, bid on "solar panel installation Dwarka", "rooftop solar Dwarka" and "solar company near me" with location targeting, and add negatives such as jobs, training, franchise, dealership and course.
  • Creatives that work locally: a short video on a Dwarka-area rooftop, a before-and-after bill (with the customer's permission), and a plain explainer of central plus Delhi subsidy with "check your eligibility" rather than a promised amount.

For full setup, see solar lead generation in Delhi, which covers targeting by DISCOM area across the city.

sections.h2: Selling solar to Dwarka's group housing societies
sections.html:
1. Build a short list. Pick societies with large terraces and high common-area loads: lifts, water pumps, corridor and basement lighting, and EV charging if they're planning it.
  2. Get a committee slot. Ask the secretary or president for 15 minutes at the next managing committee meeting. Bring a one-page summary: estimated common-area savings, central and Delhi subsidy ("subject to current rules"), roof waterproofing plan, maintenance terms and BRPL paperwork.
  3. Arm the committee for the general body. A plain-language FAQ and a 60-second video that members can forward to the society WhatsApp group make the vote easier.
  4. Use ads only to support the pitch. A small Meta campaign shown around a society you're pitching, featuring a society plant you've built, keeps your name familiar. Don't judge it on form fills.
  5. Track each society as a deal, with meeting dates, decision-makers, proposal version and next step.

sections.h2: From enquiry to booked site survey
sections.html:
Dwarka buyers usually ask two or three installers for quotes, and the first one to reply properly often gets the survey.

  1. Call within 10 minutes during working hours. If there's no answer, send a WhatsApp message with your name, company and a request for the latest BRPL bill.
  2. From the bill, check the sanctioned load and monthly units before you suggest a size.
  3. Confirm roof rights, especially on builder floors with several owners.
  4. Offer two survey slots instead of asking when they're free.
  5. After the survey, send a written quote showing gross price, expected subsidy, net cost and the BRPL net-metering steps.

Log every lead with its source, area, house type, survey and installation. Judge channels by cost per survey and per installation, not per form fill. At scale, our solar clients typically get 20–30 leads a day and 5–10 site visits a week, and our rooftop campaigns run at ₹60–80 per qualified enquiry when they're working well. Your results will depend on budget, area and follow-up.

faqs: Which DISCOM serves Dwarka for rooftop solar net metering?

Dwarka is supplied by BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL). The customer's latest electricity bill shows the consumer number and sanctioned load, which you need before you size and apply for a rooftop system.
Can a CGHS society in Dwarka get a solar subsidy?

Yes. Group housing societies and RWAs can get central assistance for common facilities under PM Surya Ghar, and the Delhi Solar Portal lists a state subsidy of up to ₹11,000 per kWp for common areas, up to 500 kWp. Check the current rules on both portals before you quote figures.
How much subsidy do Dwarka homeowners get for rooftop solar in 2026?

The Delhi Solar Portal lists a state subsidy of up to ₹26,000 per kW for the first 3 kW, capped at ₹78,000, on top of the central PM Surya Ghar subsidy. Eligible low-consumption households may instead qualify for the DISCOM-led free route. Amounts and conditions can change, so verify them before you advertise.
What is the best way to get solar leads in Dwarka?

Keep your Google Business Profile active with Dwarka reviews and photos, run tightly targeted Meta and Google ads for independent houses with ownership and units questions in the form, and treat group housing societies as a separate committee-led sale.
